claims.text: The authoritative measurement of this trip is the GPS trace, not the bill. EV-GPS-00113 is an unimpaired 217-fix trace at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, no gaps and a longest gap of 0 seconds, and it records trace_distance_km of 20.18 km over the run from the 18:47:10 start to the 19:23:10 end. EV-FARE-00113 bills distance_charged_km of 20.2 km on the same run. Under POL-RD-01 the trace polyline figure governs the excess test and the rounded actual_distance_km on the trip record may not be cited for it, so the excess at issue can be no larger than 20.18 km less the correct baseline.

The baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal, not the solo optimal. TRP-00113 is a RYDE_POOL trip, and POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline at trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km - the pooled route quoted at match time 18:42 for Punggol to the Hougang co-rider pickup to Raffles Place - and says in terms that a claim measured against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 15.80 km solo figure in the claim text is carried for reference only. The rider accepts that distance attributable to a platform-matched co-rider collection is not a deviation, so the only excess properly at issue is what exceeds 19.40 km.

On the governing figures the excess is 0.78 km and 4.02% - the 20.18 km trace against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline - which passes neither limb of the POL-RD-01 gate, since it is neither greater than 0.8 km nor greater than 20%, and the rider does not ask the tribunal to find a deviation the arithmetic does not support. The rider's point on this claim is a measurement point only: the excess must be taken from the trace's 20.18 km and must not be inflated to the rounded 20.2 km on the fare line or to the 15.80 km solo figure.

No exculpatory clause other than POL-RD-12 is open to the driver on this record, so the remaining excess beyond the matched itinerary is unexplained by any clause he can invoke. EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has an admissibility weight of 0.0 - the impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires - so there is no traffic advisory naming the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridor in the 18:41-19:23 window and no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is available. The three messages in EV-CHAT-00113 contain no rider instruction to detour and every waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run on this record. The trip_record shows no amended pickup or dropoff and no amended optimal distance, so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-quote.

The rider's profile may not be used to load her claim. EV-RPROF-00113 records deviation_claims_60d of 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, far below the four unsubstantiated claims POL-RD-08 requires before a sub-30% claim must be corroborated beyond the trace, so no enhanced corroboration burden attaches to this rider; and under POL-GEN-01 every other field on that profile - prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags, rating and the rest - is context only and cannot ground an adverse finding against her.

claims.text: The baseline for this trip is the matched pooled itinerary, not the rider's solo distance. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 optimal is trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km. The governing actual figure is the GPS trace: derived.deviation.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km, giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal (3.88 km) AND 0.8 km absolute. 0.78 km clears neither limb and misses the absolute limb by 20 metres. No deviation is established, and under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The rider's 15.8 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried on the record for reference only. Under POL-RD-12 a claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 4.4 km shortfall the claim_text asserts (20.2 minus 15.8) is an artefact of that mis-citation, not of anything the driver did. Both figures are on EV-TRIP-00113 and the ruling should name them side by side so it is visible why the arithmetic changes.

The detour the rider complains of — 'the driver went off to Hougang' — is the matched co-rider pickup, and POL-RD-12 excludes it by name: distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation and is removed from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at Hougang Central for the boarding stop, consistent with a pick-up rather than a wander.

The rider was on notice before the wheels turned, so this is not a case of a route being altered behind his back. The platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001, sent 18:42:04, states 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'; the log records it read at 18:42:31, and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 19.4 km matched-itinerary figure on the trip record is the same figure the rider was quoted in the app.

The driver's counterparty statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the platform's own records: he says a second passenger was matched at Hougang and that he drove the app route, and the system notification MSG-00113-001 records that match, MSG-00113-003 records his contemporaneous explanation 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the trace shows the stop. Nothing in the admitted evidence shows the vehicle anywhere the matched pooled itinerary did not put it.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 s sampling interval — so there is no gap, jump or sampling defect under POL-RD-07. What that clean trace shows is 0.78 km and 4.02%. The threshold is not met, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause need be invoked to defeat the claim.

No driver_profile check is engaged on this trip. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and a 0.78 km excess is far below the 8.0 km / 50% material gate. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 471, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is justified.

No traffic advisory covers the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in this window — EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need one. The exoneration relied on is POL-RD-12, the platform's own matched pooled-itinerary baseline, not POL-RD-03. No closure is asserted, so the absence of an advisory costs this defence nothing; it is cited only so the absence is on the record.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown is METERED on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEPOOL, its line items reconcile, distance_charged_km of 20.2 matches the 20.18 km the trace records, erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a 3.00 pool discount was applied in the rider's favour. Every dollar charged traces to a line the rider actually consumed.

The disputed charge still stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The dispute is rider-filed, so NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative and preserves that present state — on this record the $6.00 contested stays with the driver. The driver drove the pooled itinerary the platform matched for him and quoted to the rider; the evidence does not support a refund against him, and it should not be invented to produce one.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: this was a RYDE_POOL booking, so the correct baseline for measuring any detour is the pooled itinerary the platform matched and quoted, not your own solo route. The record carries both figures: the matched-itinerary optimal is 19.40 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km, the figure the app quoted you at 18:42 with the Hougang pickup), and the 15.80 km you cite is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried for reference only. Measuring the trip the way POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-12 require, the GPS trace (the governing measurement, an unbroken 217-fix trace at 10-second cadence, no gaps) records 20.18 km, so the excess over the correct 19.40 km baseline is 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only if the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance (3.88 km here) AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. 0.78 km fails the absolute limb by about 20 metres and fails the percentage limb by a wide margin, so no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip felt. The Hougang stop was the matched co-rider pickup, which POL-RD-12 excludes from excess by name and which the app notified you of before the trip started. To the driver: nothing adverse is found against you; you drove the pooled itinerary the platform matched, and the fare breakdown shows no billing defect (no phantom gantry, no airport surcharge, and a $3.00 pool discount in the rider's favour), so no refund is due. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is absent (weight 0.0), but no closure was relied on and its absence changes nothing. The evidence the ruling rests on — the GPS trace and the trip record — both carry full weight (1.0), so the finding is not discounted.
